title: Smith Squat (Feet Forward)
summary: A Smith squat with your feet set ahead of the bar, so you can sit back and down. Compared with the standard Smith squat, it moves some of the work to the glutes.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.8 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.2 for hamstrings: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly hamstrings total.

setup.text: Set the bar on your upper back and put your feet about a foot in front of it.
Sit down and slightly back until your thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up through your whole foot.

form_cues.cue: Wider and further forward means more glutes. Narrower and under the bar means more quads.

mistakes.text: Going so shallow the quads barely bend.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where a missed rep can be set down, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less spinal loading.
Swap sheet: One side at a time, Less spinal loading, Lower loading potential.
